text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- From 1999 all tax rates should decrease. The Christian Democrats agree to sweeping tax reform at party congress in Hanover
- Members of the GKV health insurance should pay an extra 20 marks on top of their contributions from 1997 to 1999 to finance hospitals
- Daimler-Benz restructuring postponed until 1997
- Less foreign investment in first half 1996
-IG Metall wants employers to offer option of early retirement from 55
- The Free Democrats demand a sweeping reform of tenancy law
HANDELSBLATT
- Christian Democrats at party congress in Hanover approve sweeping tax reform. Junior coalition partner liberal Free Democrats welcome proposals
- Retailers hoping for increase in sales after shops can stay open longer from November 1
- Green light for ICE German express train route between Hanover and Berlin
- With Deutsche Telekom flotation daily trade volumes on Frankfurt stockmarket could increase five-fold
- Former chief bonds trader for DG Bank Friedrich Steil sentenced to jail for five years and six months for serious breach of trust
- EU law does not save all victims of fraud. No complete control of the grey market
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Christian Democrats' party congress in Hanover approves tax reform proposals. Income tax must be drastically reduced while tax benefits will be reduced
- Next "Castor" transportation of nuclear waste postponed until 1997 to medium-term storage depot in Gorleben
- Post and Postbank end row over the costs of using post office counters
- German remains second-class as tourist destination
- German retailers urged banks, insurance firms and offices also to adopt new opening hours from November 1
- Volkswagen AG loses points in the Lopez affair. Chances increase that several top VW managers will have to answer charges in U.S. court of industrial espionage and conspiracy
DIE WELT
- Christian Democrats warn that hard times are ahead. Party congress in Hanover stresses need to save and approves tax reform concept
- DG-Bank breach of trust scandal ends with jail sentences
- German tenants association expresses outrage in response to junior coalition partner Free Democrats' proposals for new tenancy law
- Supervisory board puts brakes on Daimler boss Juergen Schrempp. Plans for restructuring postponed until 1997
- IG Metall proposes new model for early retirement
- Customers are disatisfied with Deutsche Bank - survey
-- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 26097160
